problem: Calculate the moment of inertia of a circular plate that occupies the region of an annulus $D$ centered at $O$ with inner radius $1\,\text{m},$ outer radius $\sqrt{2}\,\text{m},$ and mass density $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{|xy|}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}},$ measured in $\text{kg}/{\text{m}}^{2},$ about a line perpendicular to the ring passing through a point $3\,\text{m}$ from its center.
worked_solution:
For a plane lamina of mass $M$ and a line ${l}_{M}$ perpendicular to the lamina passing through its center of mass, the parallel axis theorem states that the moment of inertia of the lamina about a line $l$ parallel to ${l}_{M}$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M,
$$

where $d$ is the distance between the lines, and ${I}_{M}$ and ${I}_{l}$ are the moments of inertia about the lines ${l}_{M}$ and $l,$ respectively.

First, notice that the region $D$ can be expressed in polar coordinates as

$$
D={(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le \sqrt{2},\,\,0\le \theta <2\pi }.
$$

Since the mass density is symmetric in $x$ and $y,$ the center of mass is at $(0,0).$ The mass density function, in polar coordinates, is given by 

$$
\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{|r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta |}{{r}^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}|\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )|.
$$

Next, we find the mass of the plate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\frac{1}{2}|\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )|\cdot r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}r\,\text{d}r\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1}{2}|\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )|\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{r}^{2}{|}_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2-1)\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =1\,\text{kg}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the moment of inertia about the perpendicular line through the center of mass is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{M} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta )\cdot {r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\frac{1}{2}|\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )|\cdot {r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}{r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1}{2}|\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )|\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{r}^{4}{|}_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(4-1)\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about a line $3\,\text{m}$ from the center of mass is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M \\  & =\frac{3}{2}+{3}^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}+9 \\  & =\frac{21}{2}\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
